question: the decoder's ceiling on the corpus's true bond classes is 34.1% clean (T83).  Is the binding constraint the model, or the label scheme's per-bond aromatic band?
method: same harness as T83: true bond graph -> _assemble_mol, head replaced by the answer.  'smiles' takes the ligand bond classes from tmqm_parsed.csv's reference SMILES via ligand-subgraph isomorphism; metal bonds keep the Wiberg class.

charge_free_subset.note: the only fair comparison.  A charged reference cannot be transferred: the decoder builds every atom with formal charge 0, so [C-]#[O+] becomes C#O and oxygen goes over-valent.

verdict.reason: the binding constraint is not the per-bond aromatic window.  98.5% of the reference SMILES are charge-separated, and the decoder has no formal-charge channel (T85).  On the 1.5% that are charge-free, relabelling is no better than the shipped band.
